:::{#thm-information-equality}
#### Mean and variance of the score

Suppose the set of possible data values does not depend on $\vth$,
and the order of differentiation with respect to $\vth$
and integration over the data can be exchanged.
Then the score has mean zero,
and its variance is the expected information:

$$\E{\score(\vX \mid \vth)} = \mathbf{0}_{p \times 1}$$ {#eq-score-mean-zero}

$$\einf(\vth) = \Covf{\score(\vX \mid \vth)} = \E{\score \tp{\score}}$$ {#eq-information-equality}

:::

::: proof
We give the proof for a scalar $\th$ and a continuous $\vX$ with density
$\p(\vx \mid \th)$;
the vector case applies the same steps to each pair of entries,
and a discrete $\vX$ replaces integrals with sums.

For @eq-score-mean-zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\E{\score}
&= \int \paren{\deriv{\th} \log \p(\vx \mid \th)} \p(\vx \mid \th) \, d\vx
&& \text{(definition of expectation)}\\
&= \int \frac{\deriv{\th} \p(\vx \mid \th)}{\p(\vx \mid \th)} \p(\vx \mid \th) \, d\vx
&& \text{(chain rule for $\log$)}\\
&= \int \deriv{\th} \p(\vx \mid \th) \, d\vx
&& \text{(cancel $\p(\vx \mid \th)$)}\\
&= \deriv{\th} \int \p(\vx \mid \th) \, d\vx
&& \text{(exchange derivative and integral)}\\
&= \deriv{\th} 1
&& \text{(a density integrates to 1)}\\
&= 0
\end{aligned}
$$

For @eq-information-equality,
differentiate the identity
$0 = \int \paren{\deriv{\th} \log \p(\vx \mid \th)} \p(\vx \mid \th) \, d\vx$
from the first line with respect to $\th$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
0
&= \int \deriv{\th}\sb{\paren{\deriv{\th} \log \p(\vx \mid \th)} \p(\vx \mid \th)} d\vx
&& \text{(exchange derivative and integral)}\\
&= \int \paren{\frac{\partial^2}{\partial \th^2} \log \p(\vx \mid \th)} \p(\vx \mid \th) \, d\vx
 + \int \paren{\deriv{\th} \log \p(\vx \mid \th)} \deriv{\th}\p(\vx \mid \th) \, d\vx
&& \text{(product rule)}\\
&= \E{\hess} + \int \paren{\deriv{\th} \log \p(\vx \mid \th)}^2 \p(\vx \mid \th) \, d\vx
&& \text{($\deriv{\th}\p = \paren{\deriv{\th}\log \p} \p$)}\\
&= \E{\hess} + \E{\score^2}
&& \text{(definition of expectation)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So $\einf(\th) = \E{-\hess} = \E{\score^2}$,
and because $\E{\score} = 0$,
$\E{\score^2} = \E{\score^2} - \sqf{\E{\score}} = \Var{\score}$.
:::
